newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bond issuance pushes up Israel's foreign debt.
newsitem.headline: Bond issuance pushes up Israel's foreign debt.

text.p: Israel's public sector gross foreign debt in the first quarter of 1997 rose to $26.15 billion from $25.53 billion at the end of 1996, the Bank of Israel said on Sunday.

The central bank attributed the rise, which follows an increase of $1.4 billion in all of 1996, to the issuance of tradeable bonds in international markets. Since the end of 1995 the government has offered both Yankee bonds and Eurobonds.
Since the beginning of 1996 the government has also raised $2.5 billion with the backing of U.S. loan guarantees.
The public sector's gross foreign debt in 1996 equalled 26 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), against 27 percent in 1995 and about 70 percent in the mid 1980s.
The Bank of Israel said the decline in the ratio of foreign debt to GDP was a result of growth in GDP and a real appreciation of the foreign exchange rate.
Israel's net foreign debt, including both public and private sector, totalled $20.375 billion at the end of March 1997, little changed from $20.34 billion at the end of 1996.
Gross foreign debt amounted to $48.94 billion at the end of March, up by $925 million from the end of 1996.
